title: The Blaschka Object Network — Commercial Intermediary and Transport Archive Register
scope: Named non-dealer commercial actors that handled Blaschka orders after or alongside the dealer layer: forwarding agents, carriers, banking/payment intermediaries, travelling preparators, and route infrastructure. The register links explicit Blaschka transaction evidence to archival repositories where the intermediary's own paperwork may survive.
methodological_guard: Dealer, forwarding agent, carrier, bank, travelling preparator, and museum receiver are distinct roles even when one actor performs several functions. An archive of a carrier or bank is a retrieval target only when the Blaschka transaction independently documents that actor. Corporate archive survival does not prove that the relevant shipment, bill, or account row survives.

status_vocabulary.direct_transaction_actor: Named in Blaschka workshop or receiving-side evidence as participating in a specific transaction.
status_vocabulary.corporate_archive_identified: A surviving archive of the intermediary has been located, but the Blaschka transaction has not yet been isolated inside it.
status_vocabulary.distributed_or_unresolved_archive: The actor is securely named in the transaction but no dedicated archival fonds has yet been located.
status_vocabulary.candidate_successor_archive: A later or successor-company archive is historically connected but requires proof that earlier records were inherited.

routes.transaction_evidence: Primary Blaschka workshop correspondence records packages LB 285–286 sent by rail from Dresden to Trieste, delivered to the Austro-Hungarian Lloyd for the next steamer to Bombay, with onward forwarding instructions to Grindlay & Groom in Bombay. The same correspondence records a sterling draft converted through a Dresden banking institution and a remaining account balance.

actors.name: Austro-Hungarian Lloyd / Österreichisch-Ungarischer Lloyd
actors.transaction_detail: Workshop correspondence names the Lloyd at Trieste as carrier for LB 285–286 to Bombay.

archive.repository: Civico Museo del Mare di Trieste
archive.collection: Archivio del Lloyd Triestino di Navigazione
archive.guard: The archive description establishes corporate record survival. No manifest or bill of lading for LB 285–286 has yet been identified.

actors.name: Grindlay, Groom & Co., Bombay
actors.transaction_detail: Workshop correspondence gives separate forwarding instructions to Grindlay & Groom in Bombay for the Jeypore glass models.

archive.collection: Grindlays and Company: Accounting and Financial
archive.corporate_history_note: The catalogue states that Grindlay & Co opened branch firms at Calcutta in 1854 and Bombay in 1865; these became directly administered branches in 1908.
archive.guard: The surviving London sub-fonds is evidence for Grindlays corporate/accounting survival, not yet proof that Grindlay, Groom & Co.'s 1887 Bombay forwarding transaction is present in the ledgers.

additional_archive_context.guard: Too late for the 1887 transaction; retained only as successor-company archival context.

actors.name: Dresden banking institution
actors.transaction_detail: Workshop OCR records a £18 draft converted to approximately 365 Reichsmarks by a Dresden bank before deduction of the Jeypore account balance.
actors.identity_guard: The OCR wording 'Dresden Bank' is not silently normalised to Dresdner Bank AG without image-level verification.

archive_lead.guard: This is only a candidate if original-image verification establishes Dresdner Bank AG as the institution named in the Blaschka correspondence.

routes.transaction_evidence: Primary workshop OCR records one case marked I.B. 268 containing Liverpool Museum models and sent toward Hamburg through M. O. W. Möller before onward movement to Liverpool.

actors.name: M. O. W. Möller, Hamburg
actors.transaction_detail: Named in the workshop dispatch record as the Hamburg forwarding point for case I.B. 268.
actors.archive_status: No dedicated company archive or confidently identified business fonds has been located in the public-catalogue searches completed to date.

discovery_leads.research_use: The 1887 address-book run is available and can be used for name, firm, occupation and address verification; the exact M. O. W. Möller entry has not yet been isolated.

actors.guard: Do not identify M. O. W. Möller with a modern Möller forwarding company or another Hamburg Möller without a contemporary directory match.

routes.transaction_evidence: Auckland correspondence and collection research reconstruct seven Ward-supplied Blaschka models delivered by Charles Francis Adams and a triangular £20 settlement linking Auckland Museum, Adams, Ward and Ward's Australian creditor.

actors.name: Charles Francis Adams
actors.role: travelling preparator, physical carrier and payment intermediary
actors.transaction_detail: Adams is reported as safely delivering the models to Auckland and participating in the multi-party settlement through which museum funds were credited against interconnected debts.

archive.repository: Auckland War Memorial Museum manuscript collections
archive.guard: This is not an Adams personal/business fonds. It records his intermediary role from the museum/dealer correspondence side.

route_archive_priorities.target: Archivio del Lloyd Triestino di Navigazione, Trieste
route_archive_priorities.question: Can LB 285–286 be connected to a steamer, bill of lading, freight charge, sailing date, cargo manifest or Bombay arrival record in spring 1887?
Do 1887 Bombay branch/firm entries retain Jeypore Museum, Hendley, Damon, Blaschka, freight, commission or forwarding charges?

route_archive_priorities.target: Hamburg address books and commercial directories, 1886–1888
route_archive_priorities.question: Who exactly was M. O. W. Möller, what business category and address did the firm use, and can that identity lead to a company or shipping archive?

route_archive_priorities.target: Original Rakow image for the Jeypore bank conversion line
route_archive_priorities.question: Does the manuscript name Dresdner Bank AG or another Dresden banking house? Only after this identification should a bank archive be queried.

network_observation: The circulation archive is structurally wider than the dealer archive. Workshop records name actors that disappear once a museum accession is treated as the endpoint: railway freight, commercial forwarders, ocean carriers, agency houses, banks and travelling preparators. Reconstructing these actors makes logistics a documented chain of institutions rather than a generic verb such as 'shipped'.
